status: FROZEN before any of the four runs is trained and before any forecast of them exists. The SHA-256 of this file is recorded in the commit that froze it. Amendments only before any result is seen.
title: Does Pavo + spectral beat the control arm + spectral on other training draws? Three seeds of each
origin: Pavo + spectral (tailCfft2000) beat the control arm with the spectral term (controlfft2000) at 20 mm after calibration, -0.00080 [-0.00123, -0.00038] (-3.9 %), on one pair of runs, both on seed 20260909 (evaluation/pavo_spectral_plan.json). A and Pavo have each been drawn more than once and A's result wandered between draws (-6.1 % and -2.6 %, evaluation/a_replication_plan.json), so one draw per arm does not show that the gain is a property of the recipe. This plan trains both arms on two more seeds.

models.controlfft2000: seed 20260909, already trained and forecast for the test year
models.tailCfft2000: seed 20260909, already trained and forecast for the test year

pairs: Each Pavo + spectral draw is compared with the control arm + spectral draw on the same seed: tailCfft2000 with controlfft2000, tailCfft2000s2 with controlfft2000s2, tailCfft2000s3 with controlfft2000s3. The pair shares the sample order and the ensemble noise, so it differs by the tail term alone.
training: four runs, bris/slurm/finetune.sbatch with each config, on an H200 whenever one is free, two at a time at most. A run lost to the node is restarted from the beginning, unchanged. A run that does not reach step 2 000 is reported as missing and the pair is dropped from the average, with the count stated.
test: exactly as evaluation/pavo_spectral_plan.json: 2025-08-01..2026-09-06, 4 members, BRIS_LEADTIMES=7, +30 h, strict common cases of all six models and MEPS, scripts/hits_and_calibration.py --cv month --replicates 5000 --meps, one --comparator per pair. Forecasts may be split into date chunks; a final pass fills any day a chunk lost to the cluster. All six models are scored on the same days.

primary_endpoint.measure: Brier score at 20 mm per day after month-out isotonic calibration, the mean over the pairs of tail minus control: the average of the per-pair contrasts, tailCfft2000 minus controlfft2000, tailCfft2000s2 minus controlfft2000s2 and tailCfft2000s3 minus controlfft2000s3, taken day by day before the bootstrap
primary_endpoint.uncertainty: paired block bootstrap over days, seven-day blocks, 5000 replicates, with scripts/seed_contrast.py, which takes the per-pair cases already cached by hits_and_calibration.py and is written before any forecast of the new runs is scored
primary_endpoint.positive_if: the upper 95 percent bound is below 0
primary_endpoint.negative_if: the lower 95 percent bound is above 0

registered_expectation: The contrast is negative in all three pairs, and the spread of the three contrasts is smaller than the mean contrast. Reported whichever way it goes.
secondary_reported: each pair's contrast on its own, with its interval, at 20 mm; and at 10 and 50 mm
the spread of the three per-pair contrasts and of the three tail models' calibrated Brier on their own, as the plain measure of how much one draw wanders
the number of pairs, of the three, with a contrast below zero
raw Brier at 20 mm and frequency bias for each model
fair CRPS of daily precipitation over all station-days and mean precipitation relative to observed, for each pair (scripts/precip_overall.py)
2 m temperature and 10 m wind against Frost with scripts/general_skill.py (exploratory)
all six models against MEPS with four members, at 10, 20 and 50 mm
the pooled eight-member ensembles of two draws against each other (scripts/pool_seeds.py), exploratory
not_claimed: Three draws of one recipe at step 2000 on one test year, four members. Three draws give a measure of spread, not a population estimate. A pass would show the gain over the spectral control is not a property of one draw. It would not show that the spectral term adds to Pavo alone, and it says nothing about lead times beyond +30 h.
